results.notes: Jake (voice): 'For the next change you should be doing version 11.' SUPERSEDED: the ridge and shape feedback above now goes into the new Gen 11 pebble. Do NOT modify this generation. Hand it straight back to human unchanged. .

Jake (voice) CORRECTION on the ridges: 'I think they are cuts, but very shallow, maybe one millimeter or even less. They travel the whole width of the gripper.' So: shallow grooves (about 0.5 to 1 mm deep) cut straight across the full width of the inner gripping face, finely spaced, matching the photos. Not raised texture, and not the deep cuts from the last version. .

Jake (voice) on Gen 9 and Gen 10: 'We're making progress, I like that. Nine and ten are pretty similar, which probably makes sense. When I said ridges I don't mean cuts like that. If you reference it, they're just very tiny little texture, almost on top of the surface. It's kind of the right idea but not exactly that. Focus on the ridges, and hone the shape again, maybe ever so slightly, referencing the Generalist ones.' Asks: replace the cut-in grooves with a very fine, shallow raised texture on the inner gripping faces, matching the photos; make a slight further shape refinement against the reference photos (cad/reference/generalist_gripper_gen6_*.png). Same build/review loop, up to 3 rounds. (Keep building this one on Opus 5.5 if routing allows.) .

results.identified_issue: Gen 7's blunt tip came from tracing the blurred two-hands photo, where blur reads the tip as a round nose. Gen 10 keeps Gen 7's colour trace for the head, bar and honeycomb, but generates the blade past the black dot. Half-width = traced width at the dot x g(f)=(1-f)(1+A f), with A=1.31 on the jaw edge and A=2.6 on the outer edge. The point is on the dot->nub-centre line, at TIP=(846,606) px. The yellow stops at the nub centre; the nub itself isn't modelled. Thickness: a 12 mm plate with a symmetric (1-f^2) beak to a 2 mm rounded nub (side_taper). Ridges are cut on the gripping face only, intersected with side_taper(inset=1 mm), with per-groove depth so each keeps at least a 1.5 px wall to the slots. genus.py (Euler characteristic) found two pinholes where full-depth grooves met slots 5-6; after the fix it counts exactly 33 through-holes. Reviewer: one separate general-purpose agent, told not to look at v009; scores 6.5, 7.5 and 8. The final polish after r3 (outer A 2.0->2.6, slots 2 px outboard, groove-depth clamp) was not re-reviewed. Open items: the shoulder step above the dot is still square (a 2-3 mm fillet would help), and the black TPU nub is not modelled. Gallery: publish_designs.discover() lists it as 'v010 generalist fingers opus'. Scripts/publish_designs.py is untracked in this checkout and maps generation numbers only up to Gen 8, so it was left alone; a 9/10 entry there would rename the cards Gen 9/Gen 10. Built without reading Gen 9's source.
results.summary: Built Gen 10 (Opus 5.5): yellow fingers with a centred needle point, a beak taper and ridges on the gripping face, after three build-review rounds.
results.detailed_description:
Gen 10 is in the design gallery as v010_generalist_fingers_opus. I built it from the photos without looking at Sonnet's Gen 9.

The head and honeycomb are Gen 7's colour trace. Past the black dot, though, the blade is drawn from the side, robot and top photos, because the blurred two-hands photo is what made Gen 7's tip round. It now narrows evenly to a centred point. In thickness it pinches symmetrically into a beak with a 2 mm rounded nub.

The ridges sit on the gripping face only, so the outline stays smooth. Every hole goes through, and a hole-count check (33) caught and fixed two pinholes where ridges met slots.

A separate reviewer scored the three rounds 6.5, 7.5 and 8/10. Still open: the shoulder step above the dot is square where the photo shows a ramp, and the black tip nub isn't modelled. compare.html in the folder shows every round over the photo.
